title: Runtime memory surgery and KV coalescer fix for cross-env OOMs & fragmentation
creator: Aisha Palmer
description:
Summary:
Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated experienced GPU OOMs and long-tail latency spikes correlated with high KV cache churn and allocator fragmentation. This ticket tracks a runtime patch (KV coalescer + slab compaction heuristics) to mitigate leaks, reduce KV handle churn, and reclaim fragmented arenas without full process restarts.

Impact and customer escalations:
- Hosted: two medium-tier customers observed ~3x OOM frequency during sustained chat workloads (40–80 concurrent sessions).
- Dedicated: one enterprise tenant reported repeated pod restarts on 8-GPU nodes after model switchovers; tail latency increased 95th->99th percentile.
- Private: on-prem customer saw memory plateauing over several days leading to manual restarts.

Investigation log (chronological):
- 2026-02-20: First SE report from Hosted customer A (support ticket 47211) — OOMs post model warmup. Reproduced in staging with long prefix sequences.
- 2026-02-23: Heap profile captured (heap_profile_0223.pb) — shows many small KV handle allocations never freed; slab arenas showing 40% unusable fragmentation.
- 2026-02-25: Kernel scheduling analysis ruled out GPU driver regression; host memory pressure observed only after sustained KV growth.
- 2026-02-26: Internal load test (kv_churn_test_v3) reproduced the fragmentation pattern by doing repeated session create/destroy with mixed-length prompts.
- 2026-02-28: Customer escalations consolidated; decision to develop a targeted runtime patch (coalescer + on-demand slab compaction) and short-term mitigations.

Root cause hypothesis:
- KV cache handles created during session turn-taking were not coalescing due to a race when sessions terminate concurrently. The allocator leaves partially-used slabs which the GC did not reclaim quickly, incrementally increasing fragmentation until OOM.

Short-term mitigations already deployed:
- Hosted: rolling limit on concurrent session pre-warm per node (config override) to reduce churn (rolled 2026-03-02).
- Dedicated: emergency autoscaling rule to prefer lower-density node placement for affected tenants (config change PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/6127).
- Private: support playbook updated with manual slab compaction command and telemetry extraction steps (confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/KV+Mitigation+Playbook).

Patch plan (what we're building):
1) KV coalescer: a safe merge pass on session teardown that collapses adjacent KV handle fragments belonging to the same model/namespace. This reduces the number of live handles and amortizes allocation overhead.
2) Slab compaction heuristic: an on-demand compaction triggered when fragmentation > 25% and free memory below node-specific threshold. Compaction runs as a low-priority background task and yields to inference.
3) Guardrails: patch includes feature flags to toggle coalescer and compaction, and a canary rollout path per cluster tier.

Engineering progress and decisions:
- 2026-03-03: Design review with infra and runtime teams — consensus to implement coalescer in C++ runtime layer rather than Python shim to avoid GC pauses. Action: ENG-26102 assigned for implementation details.
- 2026-03-05: Prototype coalescer landed in feature branch (github.com/redwood/repo/compare/kv-coalescer-proto). Early microbenchmarks: reduces handle count by ~35% on churn workload.
- 2026-03-08: Slab compaction algorithm v1 implemented; initial integration tests show 20–30% reclaimed memory with <3% throughput regression.
- 2026-03-10: Security review triage — compaction touches allocator internals but does not access customer data. Determined that standard SRE sign-off is sufficient (security_review_required: false).

Testing and rollout strategy:
- Canary: 5% of Hosted nodes (non-production tier) enable feature-flagged runtime (runtime-1.21-canary). Monitor OOM rate, 99th latency, and allocator metrics.
- Dedicated: manual opt-in for one pilot customer node group; run for 72 hours before wider rollout.
- Private: ship as patch + instructions for onsite testing; coordinate with support before enabling.

Open risks and mitigations:
- Compaction CPU overhead under extreme load: mitigation — back-off compaction frequency and instrument preemption points.
- Race conditions during coalescer merge: mitigation — add per-bucket locks and fuzz-testing harness (kv_fuzz_v4).
- Potential regressions in latency-sensitive customers: mitigation — canary plus automatic rollback if 99th latency increases >10%.

Acceptance criteria for release:
- OOM frequency reduced by >=70% on reproduced workloads in staging.
- No more than 5% throughput regression in end-to-end generation for standard benchmarks.
- Canary stable for 72h with no manual rollbacks and no increase in sev2 reports.

Links and artifacts:
- Incident dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/redwood/runtime-ooms-kv/overview?from=now-30d
- Playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/KV+Mitigation+Playbook
- Prototype PRs: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/6127, https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/6193
- Heap profiles: s3://redwood-logs/heap_profiles/heap_profile_0223.pb

Next steps (owners):
- Luca Fernandez: finish unit tests for coalescer and land PR (target 2026-03-16).
- Maya Chen (SRE): prepare canary wave and dashboard alerts (target 2026-03-18).
- Solutions/Support: draft customer communication template for pilot customers (target 2026-03-14).

Notes and follow-ups:
- Consider adding continuous KV-handle accounting to the console (future work) to detect growing handle counts before fragmentation hits OOM.
- Evaluate long-term allocator redesign in runtime-2.0 planning cycle if fragmentation regressions persist.
